clue.text: Reversing second nought and another nought equals four

indicators.note: the opening word tells the solver to read the whole string built from the following pieces backwards

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in units of time
owt is northern English dialect, used here loosely for nothing (strictly nowt)
a second helping of the same dialect word for nothing

explanation.surface: A mathematical riddle: some reversal of noughts somehow adds up to four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns the whole of S + OWT + OWT backwards. OWT is Yorkshire dialect, normally meaning 'anything'; the setter stretches it to 'nought', which the blogger questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of twos sums to four, so the phrase is a jokey equivalent of the number.

clue.text: Satnav detailed rocks hemming in mountain peak explorer

indicators.note: hemming in means surrounding, so the jumble encloses the next piece
rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the trimmed letters are jumbled
read as de-tailed: the word Satnav loses its final letter
the peak of the word mountain is its top, that is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sat-nav has been wrecked on rocks while guiding someone round a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means de-tailed, dropping the V of SATNAV; 'rocks' scrambles SATNA into TASAN, and 'hemming in' puts M (the 'peak' of 'mountain') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch seafarer who charted Tasmania and New Zealand, a famous explorer.

clue.text: Figure it's what covers Wimbledon etc with pine

parts.note: an outside broadcast, abbreviated OB, is how television covers events such as Wimbledon
to pine is to long or yearn for something

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what shape the tennis coverage takes, with a pine tree thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; OB (outside broadcast) is a television term for coverage from a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is a geometric shape, a figure in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: One skilled in movements gets cake warm (outside temperature hot but not connected)

indicators.note: gets is read loosely as becomes, the pooled letters turning into something new
not connected suggests the letters are disjointed and come apart from their order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A bakery instruction: warm the cake, but not while the oven is plugged in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'but not connected' rearrange CAKE WARM together with T and H; 'outside' only says the abbreviations join the pool. 'Movements' misleads toward dance or politics; it means clockwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch's movement is its internal mechanism, so a craftsperson who builds these mechanisms is skilled in movements.

clue.text: Amounts to being elevated alongside live forecaster

indicators.note: in a down clue, being raised means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: amounts to means is, as in two and two is four
by means next to or alongside
L is short for live, as on electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's figures rise while living well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being elevated' reverses IS to SI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical legend a sibyl was a prophetess, someone who foretold the future.

clue.text: Modish computer element inserted in top fairy transport

indicators.note: inserted in means the next pieces are put inside the fairy's name

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, mentioned in Romeo and Juliet
in means fashionable or modish
IC stands for integrated circuit, a component of a computer

explanation.surface: A trendy chip goes into a fairy queen's magical carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small taxi booked by phone is a common form of hired transport.

clue.text: Maria, root out stays!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of Maria and root are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone tells Maria to dig out the corset stays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' looks like corsetry or a verb; it is a plural noun meaning postponements.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a suspension or postponement; a stay of execution is a legal delay.

clue.text: No need to be more explicit about entertainment fads designed to take one in

definitions.text: No need to be more explicit

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for entertainment is reversed

parts.note: fun is entertainment or amusement

indicators.note: take ... in means the arranged letters enclose the next piece
with take, in says one piece goes within another
designed suggests the letters of fads are arranged anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Trendy fads in entertainment are made to deceive, and that is all there is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about', 'designed' and 'take ... in' are the indicators; 'entertainment' looks like part of the definition but supplies the reversed piece. The phrase is a colloquial clipping of 'enough said'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial for enough said: the point is obvious and further explanation is unnecessary.

clue.text: Soft copper ring in gleaming setting

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: a ring placed in a setting goes inside it
the shining word acts as the setting that holds the ring

parts.note: shiny means gleaming
O resembles a ring in shape

explanation.surface: A soft copper ring sits in a shiny jewellery setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and well padded, like a cushion; a descriptive adjective for yielding texture.

clue.text: Infamous, rather theatrical, start of assault on Everest?

parts.note: base means ignoble, low or shameful
camp means exaggerated and theatrical in manner

explanation.surface: A melodramatic, notorious beginning to an attempt on the world's highest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers set out from a fixed lower encampment, so it is where a mountain ascent begins; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Rent here in southern Europe

definitions.meaning: rent here is a noun, a tear or rip
a port city on the Croatian Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: Someone renting a place in southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for lodging; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear or crack matches the first sense; the second is a Dalmatian coastal city in Croatia.

clue.text: Gloves are off when first base abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A baseball moment: the gloves come off when first base is left empty.
explanation.walkthrough: First base is a baseball position, which makes the gloves look like fielding mitts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting without boxing gloves means using naked hands, the gloves-off idiom taken literally.

clue.text: Remove all trace of one with two names (one hot, one defunct)

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
N abbreviates name, so two of them give NN
I is the Roman numeral for one
H abbreviates hot, as on a tap
again the Roman numeral for one
late means dead or defunct

explanation.surface: Erasing someone with two names, one fiery and one deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out utterly, destroying something so that no trace is left.

clue.text: See 24
Cleric's office bloke located at York, say, losing it

parts.note: chap is informal for a man or bloke
lain, past participle of lie, as in where something has lain or been situated

indicators.note: losing means the following short word is taken out

parts.note: York is an example of a city
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man based in York leaves his church post after losing his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks York as an example of a CITY; 'losing' drops IT to leave CY. The blogger thought 'located' a loose fit for LAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The post or office held by a clergyman attached to an institution such as a hospital or college.

clue.text: Snapping flower in rain hurt stem tip badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of in rain hurt are messed up
the tip of stem is its end, its last letter

explanation.surface: A flower damaged in the rain, its stem snapping at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapping' looks like breaking stems; it alludes to the snapdragon's flowers, which open like jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for the snapdragon, whose blooms snap open when squeezed.

clue.text: Names of two females and male finally getting bit parts in a picture

parts.note: Tess is a woman's name
Ella is a second woman's name

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word male

explanation.surface: Two actresses and a man end up with minor roles in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit parts' and 'picture' suggest cinema; a picture here is a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tiles that make up a mosaic image are the pieces of a picture.

clue.text: Piece of armour Shakespeare placed round topped and tailed fish

indicators.note: placed round means the playwright's title goes around the next piece

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare's familiar title

indicators.note: topped and tailed means the fish loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish

explanation.surface: Shakespeare garnishes a fish whose head and tail have been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' strips W and E from WRASSE, leaving RASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate protecting the upper arm in a suit of armour; the word now also means an armband.

clue.text: Absolutely necessary to score goal: bit wayward with ball

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so the letters of goal and bit wander

parts.note: O looks like a ball

explanation.surface: A footballer's wayward goal: a slightly off-target shot with the ball still scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like scoring a goal; it is a musical score. This spelling is a variant; the usual one has two Bs.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical instruction for an accompanying part that is essential to a piece and must be played.

clue.text: Routinely approve of card games with pack

parts.note: rubbers are sets of games in bridge or whist
to tamp is to pack down tightly

explanation.surface: Nodding through a deck of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official sanction automatically, without proper scrutiny, like an office stamp.

clue.text: Fly in strict set sequence

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An insect flying in a precise ordered pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Namely, it will cover Dolly's bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Dolly's bosom will be covered, that is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks anatomical but means broken. The definition plays on 'Names', the investors who underwrite the London insurance market.
explanation.definitionFit: The London insurance market covers risks, backed by investors known as Names; hence 'Name-ly' insurer.

clue.text: See 6
Bone fused at least with arm

indicators.note: fused means melted together, so the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken bone, fused at least with the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five long bones of the foot between the ankle and toes.

clue.text: Fictional character from penny-dropping tragedy

indicators.note: dropping means losing the coin letter from the front

parts.note: pathos is the tragic quality that stirs pity

explanation.surface: A character created when the penny drops in a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penny-dropping' looks like the idiom for sudden understanding; it means P removed.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Dumas's Three Musketeers, a character in a novel.

clue.text: Grand, historic, upstanding police force accepting service's premier award for record success

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
old means historic

indicators.note: accepting means the reversed force takes in the next letter
upstanding, in a down entry, means written bottom to top

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a British police branch

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letter of service's

explanation.surface: An honest, venerable police force receives top honours for a successful record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' turns CID into DIC; 'accepting' puts S (the 'premier' letter of 'service's') inside. 'record' looks like a track record; it is a music recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A framed disc presented to artists when a recording reaches a certain sales level.

clue.text: Religious leader has a duty to inculcate nursemaid

indicators.note: to inculcate is to instil, so these pieces are put into the nursemaid

parts.note: an ayah is a nanny or nursemaid in South Asia
a toll is a charge or duty

explanation.surface: A cleric has a responsibility to teach the nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Shiite Muslim cleric in Iran, a religious authority.

clue.text: Out to lunch, Brazil fashion?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for crazy or eccentric
like a Brazil, a kind of nut

explanation.surface: Away at lunch, dressed in Brazilian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' looks like the country; it is the Brazil nut, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad covers the first sense; the second is literal, resembling or full of nuts.

clue.text: Opening date that is desperate

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An opening date that is a frantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-or-nothing, frantic attitude that risks everything to succeed.

clue.text: Reserve cast head

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A reserve player is thrown in head first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a substitute or booking; it is the quality of being reticent.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence, a reluctance to put oneself forward.
